Hi Marissa,

Thanks for taking this up. We're finishing our vendor security review and have a few specific items in the attached SSQ about telemetry and PII handling for LLM-enabled features. High level asks:

1) Can you confirm which telemetry streams (inference inputs, logs, metrics, traces) may contain customer PII and where each stream is routed (hosted, dedicated, private)?
2) For hosted customers, how is tenant segmentation enforced at the network and storage layer? Any examples of ACLs, VPC routing, or zone isolation?
3) Retention controls: are there tenant-level retention policies and self-service deletion APIs, and how do they interact with dedupe/caching layers?
4) KMS custody: which keys are customer-managed vs Redwood-managed for logs/backups? Any HSM integrations?
5) Can you provide a simplified dataflow diagram showing ingress -> inference -> telemetry export -> storage (and which subsystems see cleartext PII)?

We've attached our SSQ (healthsync-ssq-v2.pdf) for reference. Can we target a response by 2026-11-02? If you prefer, a quick 30-minute call this week works.

On Tue, Oct 26, 2026 at 14:03 Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com> wrote:
> Quick clarifying question: when you say "telemetry export" ...

FWIW, here's the short answers I recommend we send back (technical):

- Telemetry streams that may include PII: inference inputs (if customer sends user text), request-level logs (errors that include full prompt), and retention-enabled transcripts. Metrics and aggregated traces (latency histograms, token counters) are never storing PII by design.

- Routing: Hosted API customers' request/response flow stays in Redwood's hosted infra unless they opt for Dedicated or Private. Tenant segmentation uses namespace isolation at the routing layer + per-tenant storage buckets. For hosted: data lives in per-tenant storage prefixes (s3://redwood-hosted/tenants/<tenant-id>/) with IAM policies scoped. For Dedicated: data remains in customer's reserved GPU pool and tenant buckets with strict network ACLs.

- Enforcement: We enforce segmentation via (1) request routing by tenant token -> compute pool, (2) per-tenant object prefixes + IAM role scoping, (3) VPC peering and security groups for Private deployments. Example ACL snippet: 'arn:aws:s3:::redwood-hosted/tenants/123/*' with role redwood-tenant-123.

- Retention: We expose per-tenant retention in the Console and an API (DELETE /v1/tenant/{id}/data?older_than=...). Caching layers (KV/prefix caches) are tenant-scoped and honor retention windows; we perform async eviction within 24h of policy change.

- KMS: Logs/backups default to Redwood-managed KMS keys (alias/redwood/ssq-logs). Customers on Private or with enterprise KMS subscriptions can provide CMKs (bring-your-own-key) and we support AWS KMS, GCP CMEK, and HSM via Vault.

I also uploaded a simplified dataflow diagram to Drive: https://drive.redwood.com/drive?file=segmentation-diagram-20261027 (redwood-pii-segmentation.png)

Hi Elena,

Thanks for the patience — please find our answers below and attached artifacts (redwood-ssq-answers.docx, redwood-pii-segmentation.png). We've answered the specific SSQ sections where relevant and added implementation notes.

Key points:
- Inference inputs and request-level logs are the only telemetry that can include PII; metrics/traces are pseudonymized/aggregated.
- Hosted customers: tenant data is isolated via per-tenant object prefixes and IAM scoping; we do not co-mingle tenant objects in the same prefix.
- Retention: tenant-level retention policies available via Console/API. Cache eviction is tenant-aware; deletion requests propagate to persistent storage and cache within 24h.
- KMS: default Redwood-managed keys; enterprise customers can bring CMKs (AWS KMS/GCP CMEK) or use customer HSM via Vault integration.

Next steps: If these answers are sufficient, we'll mark the SSQ as 'answered' in your portal and send the formal evidence bundle. If you'd like a live walkthrough of the diagram, happy to schedule the Thu slot (10/28) or early next week.
